This appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company under Section 173 (1) of the Motor
Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 20.07.2018 passed in MACC.No.32 of 2017 by Member
M.A.C.T.,
Raisen.
2. It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that policy for the vehicle was issued by the Insurance Company from 26.10.2015 to 25.10.2016.
On the date of incident i.e. 01.12.2016 the vehicle was not insured.
The owner of the vehicle Brijesh Choubey has claimed that he had paid the premium but he has not submitted the receipt.
The insurance policy (Exhibit-D/5) submitted by the owner is fake.

It is also submitted that even in written statement Insurance Company has pleaded that at the time of incident this vehicle was not insured and policy (Exhibit-D/5) is not issued by the Insurance Company.
In this policy the date of paying stamp duty is mentioned as 31.07.2015 while it is stated that this policy was issued on 25.10.2016.
It clearly proves that document Exhibit- D/5 is false and fabricated and it has not been issued by the insurance company.
Therefore, Insurance Company is not liable.
The finding arrived by the learned tribunal is totally perverse and illegal and it is liable to be set aside.

3. It is submitted on behalf of the claimant that at the time of incident vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company and learned tribunal has passed the reasoned order and found that at the time of accident, vehicle was insured, therefore, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

5 . In this case, on behalf of the claimant (respondent nos.1-5 in the present appeal) Begum Bi (P.W-1) and witness Abdul (P.W-2) and on behalf of appellant- Insurance Company, Legal Manager Narendra Soni (DW-1) and owner of the vehicle Brijesh Choubey (non-applicant no.2 in the present appeal) have been examined before the tribunal.
Appellant/respondent no.3 Insurance Company has filed the written statement before the Tribunal.
In para 14 and in para 5 of additional pleading it has been pleaded that vehicle no.MP-40-T-0351 is not insured with the Insurance Company.
Therefore, it is clear that even in the written statement the Insurance Company/appellant has pleaded that offending vehicle is not insured with the Insurance Company.

6. It is a case of the vehicle owner/non-applicant no.2 ( respondent no.7 in the present appeal) that his vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company from 25.10.2016 to 24.10.2017 (Police No.3373/00438994/000/00).
In this regard, Insurance Policy (Exhibit-D/5) has been submitted.

Owner of the vehicle Brijesh Choubey (D.W-2) in para 2 of his evidence has stated that agent of the Cholamandalam General Insurance Company has received Rs.22,400/- from him and he has given the policy but in Para 5 of the cross-examination, he has stated that for the insurance policy, he has deposited the money in the office of the Insurance Company.

Therefore, from perusal of his statement it is found that there is material contradiction that whether he has given premium money to the agent of the company or he himself deposited the money in the office of the company which creates serious doubt on the authenticity of the insurance policy ( Exhibit D/5).
If he himself had paid the money in the office of the Insurance Company, then he should have received the receipt for the same.

Insurance Police (Exhibit- D5) has been submitted by the owner of the vehicle and according to the policy, the period is 25.10.2016 to 24.10.2017, but in the second page of the policy the date for payment of stamp duty is mentioned as 31.07.2015 which also make the authenticity of document doubtful.
7 . On behalf of owner, premium receipt has also not been submitted.
Narendra Soni (D.W-1) Legal Manager of the Insurance Company has stated that this policy has not been issued from his office.
8. The learned tribunal after appreciating the evidence of both the parties, recorded the finding that insurance policy (Ex. D/5) is genuine.
Learned tribunal did not accept the contention of the insurance company that this policy is forged and fabricated.

9. The grievance of the insurance company is that it has been held liable even though it had proved,
to the satisfaction of the tribunal, that the insurance policy submitted by the owner was forged and fabricated document.
The submission of the claimant, on the other hand, is that the insurance policy is genuine.
10. On close scrutiny, this Court finds that approach of the tribunal was wholly erroneous.
From irrefutable evidence produced before the tribunal, it had been proved that the insurance policy (Ex.D/5) was a forged and fabricated document.
It was shown on the basis of cogent evidence led that the insurance policy had actually been not issued for the relevant period.

There was no material before the tribunal on which it could be inferred that the insurance company or its agent had actually received premium for issuing insurance policy for the period in question in respect of the Branch Manager Cholamandalam Ms ... vs Smt. sentences.text: The finding recorded on basis of such unfounded assumption is perverse and cannot be upheld.

11. In the considered view of this Court, once the tribunal had been shown by irrefutable and unrebutted evidence that the insurance policy was a forged and fabricated document, there was no occasion for appellant/insurance company to be held statutorily or contractually liable to pay the compensation for or on behalf or in lieu of the owner of the offending vehicle.
The insurance company is custodian of public money and trust and cannot be called upon to indemnify those with whom it has no contractual liability.
12. With the aforesaid discussion, appeal of insurance company is allowed.

The impugned judgment,
to the extent it fastened liability on the insurance company to pay compensation to the claimant, is set aside.
At the time of filing of appeal, the insurance company has deposited 50% of awarded amount by order dated 31.10.2018.
That amount still lies with the tribunal, therefore, that amount will be returned back to the insurance company with accrued interest, if any.
But in this case non-applicant no.1/respondent no.6 Roop Singh and non-applicant no.2/respondent no.7 Brijesh Chaubey driver and owner of the vehicle will jointly be liable for the compensation.
